parts.text: 3 A student makes crystals of the salt sodium sulfate, Na 2 SO 4 . The student reacts 0.200 mol / dm 3 dilute sulfuric acid, H 2 SO 4 (aq), with aqueous sodium hydroxide, NaOH(aq). The student uses the following steps. step 1 The student places 40.0 cm 3 of NaOH(aq) into a conical flask. This volume contains 0.0100 moles of NaOH. step 2 The student adds a few drops of methyl orange indicator to the NaOH(aq) in the conical flask. step 3 The student adds 0.200 mol / dm 3 H 2 SO 4 (aq) to the flask until the end-point is reached. step 4 The student transfers the mixture from the conical flask to an evaporating basin and obtains dry crystals.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Complete the symbol equation for the reaction. Include state symbols. H 2 SO 4 (aq) + 2NaOH(aq) Na 2 SO 4 (......) + ....................(......) [2]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Calculate the concentration of NaOH(aq) used in step 1. concentration of NaOH(aq) = .............................. mol / dm 3 [1]

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Calculate the volume of H 2 SO 4 (aq), in cm 3 , added in step 3. volume of H 2 SO 4 (aq) = .............................. cm 3 [2]

parts.label: h
parts.text: (h) In step 4, the student gently heats the solution in the evaporating basin until the solution is saturated. The student then stops heating and leaves the hot solution to cool. Crystals start to appear.
